name: Agent Workflow Memory
authors: Zora Zhiruo Wang, Jiayuan Mao, Daniel Fried, Graham Neubig (Carnegie Mellon University; MIT)
venue: ICML 2025 (PMLR v267, pp. 63897-63911); arXiv preprint (submitted Sep 2024)
feedback_source: self-generated; in the online setting an LM-based evaluator (AutoEval-style binary success judge from Pan et al. 2024) gates which self-generated trajectories are kept; in the offline setting canonical human-annotated training trajectories are used as the source of experiences
iteration_structure: iterative-refine (streaming continual learning: induce-integrate-utilize loop over a stream of tasks; offline variant is a single up-front induction pass over training examples)
reflection_object: reusable skill/workflow (also prompt/context): AWM reflects on past action trajectories to abstract commonly reused routines ('workflows') and injects them into the agent's text memory/context to guide future actions; it does not modify the model's reasoning chain in-flight nor update weights
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge / separate retrospective LM evaluator (online setting uses an LM-based binary success evaluator following Pan et al. 2024 / AutoEval to filter trajectories before inducing workflows); no trained reward model and no verifiable execution reward is used to gate induction
distillation_target: reusable-skill/workflow: successful experiences are distilled by an LM induction module into abstracted, parameterized workflows (NL description + sequence of observation/reasoning/action steps with example-specific values replaced by placeholders), stored in a textual workflow memory
emergent_vs_engineered: prompt/scaffold-engineered: the workflow-induction and integration behavior is built via prompting an LM to extract abstract sub-routines and by appending them to memory; it is not an RL-emergent reflective behavior
memory_type: skill-library (a workflow memory / library of induced reusable routines appended to the agent's textual memory; base memory holds documentation of built-in actions like CLICK and TYPE)
memory_persistence: cross-task (online: workflows accumulate across the stream of test tasks within a website group; offline: workflows induced from training examples are reused across all test examples). Run on a per-website basis to keep the workflow collection small and relevant
memory_curation_mechanism: self-summarized/curated plus retrieval-gated relevance: an LM abstracts and segments trajectories into fine-grained workflows (deduplicated in the rule-based variant); memory is kept small by grouping/running AWM on a per-website basis so only relevant workflows accumulate. Online induction is gated by an LM success evaluator (only success-judged trajectories are distilled). Effectively append-only with abstraction; new complex workflows are built on top of previously induced ones (snowball effect)
error_localization_granularity: step-level / block-level: workflows are induced at the granularity of reusable multi-step sub-routines (action blocks), and abstraction operates over step sequences; success/failure judgment in the online setting is holistic/outcome-level (binary task success)
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: AWM transfers distilled experience (workflows) across tasks, websites, and domains; explicitly demonstrated cross-template, cross-website, and cross-domain generalization (contrasted with intra-task refinement methods like Self-Refine)
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only: AWM does not correct a trajectory mid-flight; it improves performance on subsequent tasks by providing better workflow guidance. In the online setting only success-judged trajectories are distilled, so failed trajectories are simply not turned into workflows rather than recovered
task_domains: web-navigation (digital agents); domains covered include travel, shopping/e-commerce, social media/forum discussions, collaborative software development, content management
benchmarks: WebArena (812 tasks, 5 websites/4 domains, execution-based) and Mind2Web (cross-task, cross-website, cross-domain splits; 1000+ tasks from 200+ domains combined)
headline_result: On WebArena (online AWM, GPT-4 gpt-4-0613), 35.5% total success rate vs 23.5% for the BrowserGym baseline (+12.0 absolute, +51.1% relative), also beating SteP (33.0%, uses 14 human-written workflows) by +7.6% relative while using ~2.0 fewer steps/task. On Mind2Web cross-task offline (GPT-4), step success rate 45.1% vs MindAct 36.2% (+8.9 abs), and +24.6% relative step-wise success rate gain reported overall
baselines: WebArena: WebArena base agent (Zhou et al. 2024, 14.9%), AutoEval (Pan et al. 2024, 20.2%), BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024, 23.5%; ax-tree variant 15.0%), SteP (Sodhi et al. 2023, 33.0%, human-engineered workflows). Mind2Web: MindAct (Deng et al. 2023), Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024, retrieves concrete examples), CogAgent
gains_vs_baseline: WebArena: +12.0 absolute / +51.1% relative SR over BrowserGym (strongest autonomous baseline); +11.8 to +30.7 absolute points across the five website splits; also +7.6% relative over the human-workflow SteP baseline. Mind2Web cross-task: +8.9 step-SR over MindAct (GPT-4, 45.1 vs 36.2); generalization gains of +7.4-8.9 (cross-task), +3.6-3.8 (cross-website), +14.0-16.9 (cross-domain) absolute step-SR over MindAct; online AWM surpasses baselines by 8.9-14.0 absolute points as train-test gap widens
compute_cost_profile: Reduces, rather than increases, inference cost vs comparable methods: AWM uses ~2.0 fewer steps/task than BrowserGym on WebArena (5.9 vs 7.9 steps) and ~40.8 fewer steps on average than AutoEval (5.9 vs 46.7). Extra cost is one LM induction call per (group of) successful trajectory plus an LM evaluator call per task in the online setting; no training/gradient cost (training-free). Workflows add tokens to the context but the per-website grouping keeps memory small
known_limitations: Online induction can distill incorrect workflows from model-predicted trajectories that are wrongly judged successful, degrading performance; AWM follows workflows somewhat rigidly and agents struggle to identify when to diverge from workflow guidelines (lower action F1 vs MindAct); workflow-as-action variant (AWM_AS) is used by agents only ~18.5% of the time (resistance to new actions) and pre-determined action sequences fail under dynamic environment changes (e.g., flight-booking pop-up airports) because intermediate states are not observed; evaluated only on text-based web navigation (GPT-3.5/GPT-4), not embodied/visual or weight-update settings; offline relies on availability of distribution-matched annotated examples
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify (online) / partially oracle-dependent (offline): online AWM relies on a self-/LM-based success evaluator (no ground-truth labels) to gate which trajectories become workflows; offline AWM relies on canonical human-annotated training trajectories (a form of ground-truth/oracle supervision). No execution-based verifiable reward gates induction. The authors note imperfect online evaluation can introduce noisy/incorrect workflows
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive (and task-dependent): induced workflows consistently improve success on subsequent tasks across WebArena and Mind2Web; gains widen as the train-test distribution gap grows. However, the online setting can be net-negative on a per-workflow basis when the evaluator mislabels failed trajectories as successes, and AWM_text/AWM_AS variants sometimes trade higher step-SR for lower task-SR
calibration_effect: not-measured (paper does not report confidence calibration; it measures task/step success rate and step counts, not model calibration or a 'reasoning tax')
failure_attribution_capability: n/a (AWM is an experience-distillation/memory method, not a failure-attribution method; it does not classify failure modes or attribute responsibility to steps/agents)
failure_mode_addressed: Targets lack of cross-task reuse and inability to adapt over time (agents solving each task in isolation, not learning from past successes); related to MAST-style 'no/superficial reflection' and poor reuse of prior experience. The online variant's risk of distilling wrong workflows relates to error-propagation/noisy-memory failure modes; workflow rigidity relates to inability to recover from dynamic state changes
dataset_or_benchmark_released: No new dataset/benchmark released; evaluates on existing WebArena and Mind2Web. Releases code (and induced workflows) at https://github.com/zorazrw/agent-workflow-memory
builds_on: Reflexion-style learning-from-experience and skill/library-induction lineage: Voyager (Guanzhi Wang et al. 2024, skill library), LATM/Cai et al. 2023 and CRAFT/ASL-style LM tool/skill creation (Wang et al. 2024b/c), Synapse (Zheng et al. 2024, retrieved exemplars), MindAct/Mind2Web (Deng et al. 2023), WebArena (Zhou et al. 2024), BrowserGym (Drouin et al. 2024), SteP (Sodhi et al. 2023), AutoEval LM evaluator (Pan et al. 2024); program-synthesis library learning (DreamCoder/Ellis et al., Stitch/Bowers et al.)
extended_by_or_inspired: Cited by and related to subsequent agent-memory / workflow-induction and self-evolving agent work, e.g., Benchmarking Agentic Workflow Generation (WorfBench, arXiv:2410.07869), AgentGen / automatic agentic workflow generation, and broader 'experience-following' / skill-library memory agents (e.g., AWM appears as a baseline in later agent-memory and self-improving-agent surveys and papers). Specific successors include workflow-generation benchmarks and LLM-agent memory frameworks published 2024-2025
on_policy_distillation_link: Conceptually adjacent to on-policy distillation/skill-optimization: in the online setting AWM distills the agent's own (on-policy) successful trajectories into reusable workflows that are then re-injected to improve subsequent behavior, but the distillation is into in-context textual skills rather than model weights, and there is no gradient/policy update
sample_efficiency: Highly sample-efficient: on WebArena (map split) AWM_online reaches near-peak success after only ~40 streamed examples (fast early learning curve, gap over baseline rising as high as 22.5 points after rolling over tens of examples); requires no training data in the online setting and only the existing training set in the offline setting
